patient.chief_complaint: Progressive behavioral changes and personality shift — 18 months; referred from primary care after disability evaluation
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. R is a 57-year-old elementary school teacher currently on disability leave who presents to the cognitive neurology clinic with an 18-month history of progressive behavioral and personality changes, reported primarily by her adult daughter who accompanied her. Ms. R herself minimizes her difficulties and states that she 'just needs more rest.' Her daughter describes a woman who was formerly a dedicated and beloved teacher — organized, nurturing, and highly regarded in her community — who has undergone a profound transformation. Over the past 18 months, Ms. R has become increasingly impulsive, spending significant sums on online shopping without financial awareness or apparent concern. She has shown reduced empathy, repeatedly failing to acknowledge her daughter's distress during difficult life events and laughing at inappropriate times. She repeats the same short phrases and stories in conversation, often circling back to the same anecdote within minutes. She has been collecting cheap figurines in a compulsive fashion, filling her apartment with hundreds of identical items. She stopped attending her church, which she had done every Sunday for 35 years. Her grooming and hygiene have declined and her daughter must remind her to shower and change clothes. She was placed on disability leave 6 months ago after school parents and administrators raised concerns about her classroom behavior — she was reportedly making inappropriate personal comments to students and parents. Her episodic memory has also declined — she does not recall that her daughter was engaged until reminded, despite being told multiple times. Crucially, her brother died of ALS at age 60 six years ago. She is unaware of the genetic link between ALS and FTD. The combination of behavioral syndrome and family history of ALS raises significant concern for C9orf72-associated FTD-ALS spectrum disorder.

results.title: A hexanucleotide repeat expansion in C9ORF72 is the cause of chromosome 9p21-linked ALS-FTD
C9orf72 repeat expansion in familial and sporadic ALS-FTD

output.summary: C9orf72 GGGGCC hexanucleotide repeat expansion (>30 repeats; typically >400 in disease) is the most common genetic cause of familial FTD (25-40% of familial FTD) and familial ALS (40% of familial ALS). Key clinical points: (1) autosomal dominant with high but incomplete penetrance; (2) each first-degree child has 50% risk; (3) can present as FTD, ALS, or combined FTD-ALS in different family members; (4) anticipatory grief and family testing disclosure require genetic counselor involvement; (5) no disease-modifying therapy currently approved but ASO trials targeting C9orf72 are in Phase 1-2 trials. Pre-symptomatic testing of family members requires formal genetic counseling.
